messages.subject: modify model in HbayesDM package
parts:
Hi,

I'm Lili, a PhD student in the Insight Center for Data analytics in Dublin City University. My research is mainly about exploring how healthy people make decisions in their daily life. 

I find the package you developed is very impressive and very handy to fit the models of different tasks. My question is could I modify the model script a little bit to make it compatible with our task? You see, I'm planning to use a modified version of 2-armed bandit game, in which there's a changing probability of punishment for each choice so that people have to act to avoid getting punishment during the game (attached the paper that conducted this task in their experiments). Is there any possibility for your team to add this modified version of 2 armed bandit game into the package or is easy way to add the modified stan model file into the package by myself?

Thanks in advance!
cheers,
Lili

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Re: modify model in HbayesDM package
parts:
Hi Lili,

Thanks for your kind note. Yes you can modify the code and upload new models to hBayesDM. You can find a short tutorial here: https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/wiki.

Are you talking about the Rescorla-Wagner model or a Bayesian observer model mentioned in the paper? We plan to add Hierarchical Gaussian Filter (HGF) models in the future and the Bayesian model might be a nested model of some of HGF models. Or if you can send us some sample data from the task, it might help us implement the Bayesian model used in the paper into the hBayesDM package. Thanks!

Best,
Young

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Re: modify model in HbayesDM package
parts:
Hi Lili,

I'm sorry for this very late reply. From next year (2020), we plan to respond in a timely manner.

In step 6, basically you need to write up some codes for generating 'data_list'.

For example, if you check the 'data' block in the Stan code for the 'bandit2arm' task (https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/blob/master/commons/stan_files/bandit2arm_delta.stan), there are five variables that need to be provided by the user: N, T, Tsubj, choice, outcome. In the preprocess function, we need to specify how the five variables are generated from the raw data file (or a data.frame). 

Given the similarity of yours and the 'badnti2arm_delta' model, you can start from its template. You can see how we did it for the 'bandit2arm' task: https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/blob/2781155befd2889cafcf6336366f47f4bf392be0/R/R/preprocess_funcs.R#L4

In this code, you can probably use lines 7-11 as they are. 'subjs' are subject IDs, n_subj is the number of subjects, t_subjects is number of trials for each subject, and t_max is the maximum number of trials among all subjects. What's left to be done is how you extract info from the raw file and convert them into the five variables (N, T, Tsubj, choice, outcome).

Hope this helps and let me know if you have any further questions or need more help. Thanks!

Best,
Young
